mappings.note: Kamal Parmar's street tuition and free dinner - one person's contribution to a community's children, which CG-SST4 covers as the contributions of different sections of society.
Names the RWA as a new urban form of community; the item is about what kind of grouping has appeared, so LO-191.
A jati or its subdivision called a 'community' - a form of social grouping in the pupil's society, hence LO-191.
Identifies family life as the unit in which love and dharma are flower and fruit; the family as institution, so CG-SST4.
Defines interdependence within the family as members relying on one another - the internal working of the institution.
Parents named as those who raise children into responsible members of society; a role in the family institution.
Acchamma as the paternal grandmother - kinship vocabulary from Shalini's story, mapped with the other relationship-term items.
Tenzing's grandfather as his homework helper; a role inside the family, so CG-SST4.

An activity an RWA legislates for, such as waste or common areas: the RWA as a community type (LO-191) doing the work of a community institution (CG-SST4). Not LO-194, since an RWA is not a government body.
Communities settling practices for using shared natural wealth - a community institution regulating a common resource, so CG-SST4.
Describes the joint family and lists its members; a form of the family institution, hence CG-SST4.
Nuclear against joint family at short-answer length; the same contrast of family forms, so CG-SST4.
Why Indian kinship vocabulary is finer than English - lineage, age and gender precisely marked, reflecting the weight given to extended family, so CG-SST4.
What it signifies that cousins are called brothers and sisters; the closeness of the extended family, hence CG-SST4.
Parents' responsibilities set out at length - nurture, provision and guidance; a function of the family institution.
How children come to take part in household life through observation and graded responsibility; the family as a place of learning, so CG-SST4.
Tyaga as a family value, putting collective need before personal comfort: the family transmitting (CG-SST4) a traditional value (LO-200).
Acchamma's lesson that families share what they have in hard times - the family's mutual-support function, so CG-SST4.
How chores were shared in Tenzing's household once his mother was busy: shared responsibility (CG-SST4) and the equality question raised by a father cleaning and cooking (LO-193).
The grandfather's double role, helping at home and doing social work in the colony - family and community contribution, both under CG-SST4.
Why community members gather - festivals, weddings, farm work, crisis. The community's function, so CG-SST4.
Unwritten rules for sustainable use of water, grazing land and forest; a community institution managing common resources, hence CG-SST4.
Halma explained and then applied to the water crisis through tree planting and harvesting structures - collective community action, so CG-SST4.
Kamal Parmar's evening tuition and meals described in full; an individual's social contribution, mapped like the shorter version.
How children can shoulder family responsibilities - chores, younger siblings, elderly members; a function of the family institution.
Interdependence between communities, illustrated by residential areas depending on traders AND municipal services: the community institution (CG-SST4) and the local government's role (LO-194).
Two examples of how loosely 'community' is used - jati, a religious or regional group, a school art group. The item is about kinds of grouping, so LO-191.
Why couples now choose nuclear households: urbanisation and job mobility among the reasons, so the family institution (CG-SST4) shaped by where work is available (LO-197).
How sharing within the family teaches dana: the family as teacher (CG-SST4) of a traditional value (LO-200), like the other dana items.
Why Shalini was content with a plainer dress - she valued the whole family being clothed; family solidarity, so CG-SST4.
